speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; could you describe exactly where the pain is located and if it spreads to other joints? Also, did this start suddenly or did it develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of the finger being caught in a jersey, this sounds like a significant injury. Do you currently have any visible deformity or feel like your finger is crooked or shortened compared to the other one? Also, is there any numbness or tingling in that finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Terminal Extensor Rupture)

The clinical picture of inability to flex the DIP joint, pain localized there, and the finger resting in extension following a forced flexion injury is classic for an extensor tendon rupture. I will confirm this with imaging.
REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray_right_hand_lateral

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
